concerns.text: FR-003 states: 'System MUST split the dataset into [deferred] training and [deferred] testing sets...' The use of '[deferred]' here is syntactically inconsistent with the spec's own convention. The '[deferred]' marker is intended for empirical values (counts, percentages, thresholds) as per the 'Success Criteria' preamble, not for the existence or naming of the sets themselves. The requirement to split into 'training and testing sets' is clear; the '[deferred]' markers are redundant and confusing in this context.

The Assumptions section states: 'Publicly available datasets... contain sufficient samples (≥ 200 molecules)... to allow for a stratified 80/20 split.' This contradicts the 'Edge Cases' section which handles the scenario where 'dataset size is too small... (e.g., < 50 samples)'. While the assumption sets a target, the spec fails to define the behavior if the assumption is violated (i.e., if 50 <= samples < 200). The Edge Case only covers < 50, leaving a gap between 50 and 200 where the 'stratified 80/20' assumption might fail but no fallback is defined.
